time_basis: Current UTC clock was captured immediately before writing this review; no historical duration is inferred.

review_scope.question: Can this exact source set safely authorize the single formal C1 requested-camera numeric guard after later binding?
review_scope.method: Independent full source/protocol review plus adversarial executions confined to isolated temporary directories and pure synthetic data.

attack_checklist.attack: Recompute all four requested source identities before and after review.
attack_checklist.observation: All four SHA-256 values matched the assigned frozen values at both checks.

attack_checklist.attack: Run the built-in and independent synthetic suites under CPython 3.13.0 and 3.12.14.
attack_checklist.observation: Four isolated runs returned code 0; the exact B0 function-source hashes were stable across both interpreters.

attack_checklist.attack: Inspect formal control flow and exercise the synthetic non-consuming rejection model.
attack_checklist.observation: formal_preflight is called before commit_attempt_lease, and the synthetic rejection left no lock or staging entry.

attack_checklist.attack: Inject a post-link parent-directory fsync error during a synthetic lease commit.
attack_checklist.observation: The operation raised and still left a parseable fail-closed permanent lock receipt; no second scientific attempt was authorized.

attack_checklist.attack: Commit the same synthetic fixed lock twice.
Unlink the permanent lock path, create a different inode at the same name, and verify against the held FD.
Add a hardlink to a committed lock and separately pre-place a symlink at the fixed lock name.
attack_checklist.observation: The added hardlink was detected through st_nlink and the pre-existing symlink prevented commit.

attack_checklist.attack: Rename the opened parent directory and recreate another directory at the canonical path.
Trace every JSON/event read and attempt to identify a hash-then-path-reopen parser.
attack_checklist.observation: file_snapshot returns the exact bytes that read_json and selected_event_captures parse; tensor bodies are decoded from the same held FD snapshot.

attack_checklist.attack: Pre-place symlink and hardlink entries at a synthetic receipt path.
attack_checklist.observation: O_EXCL rejected both aliases without overwriting their targets.

attack_checklist.attack: After a synthetic PASS receipt write, rename the held output directory and create a replacement at the canonical output name, then execute the same final lock-only check used by the candidate.
attack_checklist.observation: The lock check passed although the canonical output pathname referred to a different inode and no longer contained the written receipt. The omitted output-directory lease check would have detected the swap.

attack_checklist.attack: Raise a synthetic error on the directory fsync after write_new_at has written and closed a PASS receipt body.
attack_checklist.observation: write_new_at raised, but a complete JSON body with passed=true remained visible. The receipt has no externally sealed field proving that write_new_at returned successfully.

attack_checklist.attack: In a synthetic child process, commit the default-failure lock, write a complete PASS receipt, and deliver SIGKILL before a final validation or normal return.
attack_checklist.observation: The durable state contained the unchanged default-failure lock, a complete PASS receipt, and no lock_close_failure.json. That is the same evidence tuple the protocol proposes to hand to the later reviewer, but it does not prove the guard reached its final check or returned 0.

attack_checklist.attack: Inspect nominal success ordering and late lock-failure handling.
attack_checklist.observation: The report is correctly marked pending and tensor/source checks precede its write. However, terminal PASS is published before the final lock check and process return, so the overall terminal publication is not atomic.

attack_checklist.attack: Decode a synthetic 4x4 float tensor, mutate its body through another FD, and close with verification.
attack_checklist.observation: Close verification rejected the mutation and retained truthful opened=1 and close_verified=0 counters.

attack_checklist.attack: Place a forbidden PIL pixel subtree beside selected camera fields and pass a pixel-sized tensor descriptor to the camera decoder.
attack_checklist.observation: The selector ignored the pixel subtree and the fixed shape/byte gate rejected the pixel-sized descriptor before any body open.

attack_checklist.attack: Compare the candidate against an independently transcribed left-multiply Y rotation and test wrong sign, target/cache mismatch, K drift, closure, nonfinite values, exactly 1e-6, and strictly greater than 1e-6.
attack_checklist.observation: The reference error was 0.0; the inclusive boundary passed and every negative case was rejected.

blocking_findings.finding: receipt.json can already contain passed=true before the final lock revalidation and before main returns. SIGKILL, SIGTERM, host loss, os.close failure, or directory-fsync failure in this window can leave a complete PASS receipt with an unchanged default lock and no failure marker. There is no independently written supervisor exit receipt or terminal success seal, so a later file-only reviewer cannot distinguish that interrupted state from normal completion.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Keep the worker receipt pending and add a separately supervised terminal commit that is written only after the worker exit code is observed and the lock, output-directory inode, receipt inode/content, and absence of failure markers are revalidated. Any worker-only PASS must remain non-authoritative.

blocking_findings.finding: On the nominal success path, the code performs only verify_lock_lease after writing receipt.json. It does not re-run verify_directory_lease for execution_01 and does not retain or revalidate the report/receipt file identities. A synthetic rename-and-recreate attack changed the canonical execution_01 inode after receipt publication; the candidate's final lock check still passed, so its success path can return while the canonical evidence directory is missing or replaced.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Retain exact output/report/receipt inode leases through terminal sealing, revalidate the canonical output directory and artifacts after the final write, and bind them into the external supervisor terminal receipt.

nonblocking_findings.finding: create_output_lease runs before the committed_formal_run try block. A failure after mkdir can therefore leave only the structured permanent failure lock and a partial output directory, contrary to the protocol sentence that every ordinary post-commit failure receives receipt.json. This remains fail-closed, but the protocol and implementation should be aligned during the required redesign.

authorization_effect.required_next_state: Revise terminal publication and output-lease sealing, freeze a new source identity set, and obtain two fresh different-author source reviews. This blocked review can never authorize a later revision.

evidence_boundary: This is a source-only adversarial engineering review. It establishes no C1 camera validity, score, image quality, rendered-camera obedience, method gain, causal claim, novelty, or publication-level result.
